goal:
I'm citing the 2023 paper by Bianchi and colleagues on lattice relaxation in Journal of Alpine Hydrology in my thesis: http://journal-of-alpine-hydrology.example/articles/fb8f19-scaling-laws-for-lattice-relaxation
What mean annual runoff does Table 2 report for station K-17? Please give the value with its unit and tell me which source you used.

resources.title: Scaling Laws for Lattice Relaxation
resources.version_label: Version of Record, Journal of Alpine Hydrology (2023)

paragraphs: We study lattice relaxation across five monitoring stations using a hierarchical model.
Authors: Chiara Bianchi, Uri Ibarra, Yusuf Abernathy. Published in Journal of Alpine Hydrology, 2023.
Table 2 reports the mean annual runoff for each station.
body.table_caption: Table 2: Mean annual runoff by station

sections: Abstract

We report mean annual runoff measurements from five monitoring stations collected between 2021 and 2023. A pilot survey in 2018 had put the regional mean annual runoff at 1989.4 mm; we find marked differences between upland and coastal sites.
1. Introduction
Earlier studies of lattice relaxation relied on single-site records [1, 2]. A multi-site campaign makes it possible to separate local effects from regional trends [3].
2. Methods

Station metadata are listed in Table 1. Measurements follow the protocol of [3]. Values from the 2020 campaign are given in Table 3 for comparison and are not directly comparable with the 2023 campaign because the instruments changed.
3. Results
Table 2 reports the mean annual runoff for each station in the 2023 campaign. The largest change relative to 2020 was observed at station S-12.
4. Discussion
The spread between stations exceeds the measurement uncertainty, which suggests that site conditions dominate. Longer records are needed to confirm the trend.
References
[1] Grünwald et al. (2017). [2] Fairbairn and Quiroga (2019). [3] Nakamura et al. (2020).

tables.caption: Table 3: Mean annual runoff in the 2020 campaign
